regions.merged_text: P.S. Dear Sister Agnes Carmel: After the above conclusion I read your interesting letter of April 27th last, which I should have taken time to do before writing; and again as before I would stress the necessity of humble patience -- of patient humility. Do not lament or be discouraged at your inabilities, e.g., of mixing with associates, etc. The conscientious exer- cise of the tallents God has otherwise blessed you with surely excuses you from such and ought to makeup for the former. At the same time just the weaknesses we experience -- and who is so stupid as to imagine he is an exception! -- are natur- ally providential guards against one of the very greatest dangers to genious, "the big-head". So instead of lamenting such weaknesses we really ought to thank God continually for them. In fact I believe that in the sight of Almighty God just the light to see such poverty in our own makeup and to realize thereby something of our stupidity to which sin has caused in our characters is a special grace to make us other than crazy worldlings that have no faith and never learn to really think.
